objective: Derive the conformance stale_evidence case through the shipped reducer and aging path with an explicit freshness policy and aging boundary, so the probe proves the aging boundary rather than a hand-mutated belief.
decision_supported: Should the stale dimension be produced by writing WorldBelief.LOST into a cloned state, or by aging a valid stream at an explicit boundary through age_world_state?
acceptance: The stale state is produced by reduce_events with an explicit freshness policy and aging boundary.
The probe asserts that the aging path produced LOST beliefs, not only that the verifier refused the state.
The probe detail names the boundary and the thresholds it used.
The probe event payload carries observed_at and clock_id, which the aging path reads from the payload.
The age thresholds decide the belief: 4s is observed, 20s is stale, 60s is lost.
The readiness report is regenerated and the gate tests pass.
evidence: Before the change the probe cloned a confirmed state and wrote WorldBelief.LOST into both belief maps, so age_world_state was never called.

The probe payload did not carry observed_at or clock_id, so aging produced LOST at every boundary including four seconds after the observation, which showed the thresholds were not being exercised at all.
After the change the same stream at 4s is observed, at 20s is stale and at 60s is lost, and the probe detail names the boundary and thresholds.
The full unit suite is 2280 passed, 3 skipped, which is the baseline count plus the five new tests.
stop_conditions: The aging path requires a policy the probe cannot construct for a family's entity types; the policy is built from the family's own observations, so this is not expected.
risks_and_fallbacks: The probe payload changed, so every replay_hash in the readiness report changed; the report is regenerated in the same change and the gate tests pass.

_paths.py now orders libs/kernel ahead of libs/application. Both trees contain a workbench package, and the helper's callers import workbench.kernel, so the previous order resolved to the wrong copy whenever another checkout was on the path.
